stem: Which type of color vision deficiency occurs most frequently in the human population?

options.rationale: Red-green color vision deficiency is the most prevalent form, affecting roughly 8% of males and 0.5% of females.
Blue-yellow color vision deficiency is far rarer, affecting fewer than 1 in 10,000 individuals worldwide.
Total absence of color perception (achromatopsia or monochromacy) is an extremely rare condition.
Blue-cone monochromacy is a rare inherited condition, not the most common form of color vision deficiency.

explanation: Red-green color vision deficiency (including deuteranomaly, deuteranopia, protanomaly, and protanopia) is by far the most widespread color vision defect. Because it affects roughly 1 in 12 males, digital content must never rely solely on red-green cues to convey vital information.
